sources.attribution: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, California Condor Recovery Program. 2025 Annual Population Status. Published 2026-02-25; counts as of 2025-12-31. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: As of 2025-12-31, the program counted 607 condors worldwide: 392 in the wild and 215 captive. The wild count was allocated to AZ/UT 98, California 216, the experimental Pacific Northwest population 25, and Baja 53; the disjunct PNW population is excluded from the California total.
claims.scope: Annual recovery-program accounting and its population definitions.

claims.text: The 2025 report recorded 16 wild-fledged chicks, 46 captive-to-wild releases, and 22 deaths in the free-flying wild population; nine deaths were confirmed as lead poisoning and nine awaited final necropsy.
claims.scope: One calendar/reporting year; two remote nests and early January 2026 fledging records are handled under the report's stated counting rule.

claims.text: From 1992 through 2025, 161 lead-poisoning deaths were confirmed in the wild population, equal to 50% of deaths with known cause and 28% of all wild deaths in the report's cumulative accounting.
claims.scope: Historical program totals, not a future-risk forecast.

gaps: The report is population accounting, not a formal extinction-risk assessment or population-viability analysis.
No complete species natural history or independent review is added by this page.
